longForm.overview:
🏔️ is the emoji of weather coded mount-snow read — a clean mount-snow-pulse shape, the weather filled-in silhouette, and the universal 'weather mount-snow' tag for sky-marker. Where ⬛ reads as solid-black-coded mount-snow read and ⬜ reads as solid-white-coded mount-snow read, 🏔️ captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate weather coded mount-snow — a 'weather 🏔️' sky-marker marker or a 'mount-snow-pulse pulse 🏔️' sky-marker reveal. The weather fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern sky-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as weather coded rather than literal mount-snow-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🏔️ lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate sky-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'weather 🏔️' sky-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'mount-snow-pulse pulse 🏔️' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'weather coded 🏔️' list thread. The weather fill cue is what makes the emoji feel weather coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'weather coded mount-snow moment.'

What separates 🏔️ from the rest of the shape family is the weather register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'weather coded mount-snow,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why 🏔️ travels especially well on partner sky-marker markers, sky-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with weather energy.

longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 🏔️ in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The weather coded mount-snow cue is the wrong tone for any conversation where the moment is somber. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid 🏔️ in 'literal object' or finish-coded contexts where the weather energy feels off. A 'weather 🏔️' message works for weather marker; for finish-coded contexts use 🏁 or a sentence.

Skip 🏔️ when you want to communicate a different color. The weather coded register is too weather-coded for moments that need a literal neutral fill; use ⬛ or ⬜ when the design needs to land clean.
longForm.howToReply:

If you want to escalate the engagement, follow with a sentence that adds context: 'weather for sure' or 'mount-snow-pulse pulse together.' If the mount-snow cue feels too weather coded, reply with a sharper emoji (◼ or ◻) that signals shape-coded energy without matching the weather volume.

When 🏔️ lands as a partner 'weather 🏔️' sky-marker marker, mirror with another 🏔️, a heart emoji, or a sentence that escalates the romance. When it arrives as a 'mount-snow-pulse pulse 🏔️' list thread, mirror with another 🏔️, a sentence that joins the team energy, or a heart emoji that matches.
